study_identification_part.si4_title: Comparative analysis of cortical anatomy in male participants with internet gaming disorder or tobacco use disorder: Insights from normative modeling

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To utilize normative modeling to analyze cortical thickness (CT) development patterns of male patients with internet gaming disorder (IGD) and tobacco use disorder (TUD), aiming to provide further insights into whether IGD qualifies as an addiction by comparing individual differences in brain structural features between IGD and established substance-related addiction (TUD).

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: CAT-12 toolbox; SPM-12 (Statistical Parametric Mapping version 12); Surface-based brain morphometry (SBM); Desikan-Killiany atlas parcellation (68 ROIs)
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The paper explicitly describes the preprocessing pipeline using CAT-12 integrated with SPM-12, surface-based morphometry methods, and the Desikan-Killiany atlas for cortical parcellation.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Raw MRI images were processed and analyzed using surface-based brain morphometry (SBM) pipeline available in the CAT-12 toolbox (Gaser, Nenadic, Buchsbaum, Hazlett, & Buchsbaum, 2001). The images were then integrated in the statistical parametric mapping version 12 (SPM-12) (Fig. 1B) and subjected to pre-processing steps. The volumes were subsequently segmented using surface-based and thickness estimation techniques to analyze specific regions of interest. Cortical parcellation was conducted using the Desikan-Killiany atlas (Desikan et al., 2006).

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Weighted average image quality rating (IQR) from CAT-12 with exclusion threshold of ratings below 'C-'; Euler index thresholding using site-specific median-centered approach with threshold of square root > 10; manual visual inspection of excluded participants; 8 IGD participants excluded by IQR, 2 by Euler index; 1 TUD participant excluded by IQR, 6 by Euler index; 0 HC participants excluded; Euler index included as covariate in normative modeling
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: The quality control process was performed by referring to the weighted average IQR assessed by the CAT-12 toolbox... All participants with IQR ratings below 'C-' were excluded (no participants were excluded in HC, while 8 were excluded in the IGD and 1 in the TUD). CAT-12 also calculates the Euler index... we subtracted the median Euler index of each site from every participant within it, then took the square root and multiplied by −1, and excluded participants with square roots greater than 10. Finally, we manually examined participants that exceeded the Euler index threshold to confirm their exclusion (no participants were excluded in HC, while 2 were excluded in the IGD and 6 in the TUD)... The model estimated using Gaussian process regression (GPR) generated... based on participants' age and euler index as covariates.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: ROI-level t-tests on z-scores with Bonferroni-Holm correction for multiple comparisons (p < 0.05) to determine mean group differences between cohorts; Spearman correlation coefficients (p < 0.05, FDR corrected) between regional deviations (Z-scores) and severity scores of addiction symptoms (DSM for IGD; FTND for TUD) through partial correlation analysis controlling for gender, head motion, and Euler index; visualization of regions with extreme deviations exceeding 2% threshold across groups; overlap maps calculating the proportion of extreme positive and negative deviations within each ROI across groups
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Both IGD and TUD groups exhibited widespread cortical thinning with significant overlap in bilateral temporal pole and medial orbitofrontal cortex, but TUD showed higher degree of individualization and limited spatial overlap compared to IGD, with opposite trends in CT changes between groups in bilateral pericalcarine cortex and pars triangularis.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Both addiction groups exhibited widespread cortical thinning, particularly in bilateral temporal pole and medial orbitofrontal cortex regions. Specific findings include: (1) IGD showed significant positive deviations in bilateral frontal pole (t=10.31 left, t=10.35 right, p<0.001) and right superior parietal cortex (t=3.34, p<0.001) compared to HC; (2) TUD showed significant positive deviations in bilateral frontal pole (t=4.11 left, t=6.11 right, p<0.001) and bilateral lateral occipital cortex (t=3.65 left, t=6.40 right, p≤0.001) compared to HC; (3) At z=±1.65 threshold, TUD had higher proportion of extreme ROIs (20.59% positive, 73.53% negative) compared to IGD (8.82% positive, 42.65% negative); (4) Opposite developmental trends between groups were observed in bilateral pericalcarine cortex (IGD negative deviation t=-7.82 left, t=-6.48 right; TUD positive deviation t=3.35 left, p=0.003) and bilateral pars triangularis (IGD positive deviation t=2.50 right, p=0.041; TUD negative deviation t=-4.97 left, t=-4.40 right, p<0.001); (5) Both groups showed highest negative deviations in temporal pole (IGD: left z=-1.82, right z=-1.59; TUD: left z=-2.00, right z=-2.22); (6) Symptom correlations: IGD DSM scores positively correlated with z-scores in left entorhinal cortex (r=0.27, pFDR=0.029), right lateral orbitofrontal cortex (r=0.25, pFDR=0.041), right parahippocampal gyrus (r=0.25, pFDR=0.004), and right frontal pole (r=0.26, pFDR=0.036); TUD FTND scores negatively correlated with z-scores in left lateral orbitofrontal cortex (r=-0.24, pFDR=0.047), right medial orbitofrontal cortex (r=-0.38, pFDR=0.001), right rostral anterior cingulate cortex (r=-0.28, pFDR=0.016), right rostral middle frontal gyrus (r=-0.25, pFDR=0.039), left superior parietal cortex (r=-0.29, pFDR=0.015), and left superior temporal cortex (r=-0.27, pFDR=0.023).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: ROI-wise analysis may lose local information; verbal inquiry only to exclude comorbid addictions without scale/biochemical validation; GSP dataset lacks IGD/TUD diagnoses so some participants may have these conditions; cross-sectional design limits developmental trajectory interpretation
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: Our study has some limitations. Firstly, the analysis was performed on an ROI-wise rather than vertex-wise basis. This approach facilitates comparison of structural abnormalities between regions but may result in the loss of more local information. Secondly, this study only excluded participants with other types of addiction through verbal inquiry before recruitment, lacking scale and biochemical data for intergroup comparisons. Thirdly, the GSP dataset does not provide diagnoses for IGD and TUD, so some participants in the dataset may have IGD or TUD. Despite the enormous sample size of GSP, it may still potentially affect the results of normative modeling. Lastly, the trajectory of brain development was based on the cross-sectional data, and further research is warranted to validate these findings in longitudinal cohorts.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study used overlap maps to visualize spatial convergence of extreme deviations across individuals, showing that extreme negative deviations concentrated in insula, temporal pole, and superior temporal gyrus, while extreme positive deviations concentrated in bilateral frontal pole regions. The approach demonstrated individualization patterns where TUD showed higher heterogeneity than IGD. The normative modeling framework enabled identification of both shared neurobiological alterations and disorder-specific patterns at individual level, moving beyond traditional group-level case-control comparisons.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study is notable for comparing behavioral addiction (IGD) with substance addiction (TUD) using normative modeling. Only male participants were included due to known gender disparities in prevalence. The study used multi-site GSP data for controls but single-site data for clinical groups. Diagnostic criteria for IGD: DSM-5 ≥5 criteria met and IAT score >50. Diagnostic criteria for TUD: ≥10 cigarettes/day for ≥1 year, exhaled CO ≥5 ppm, FTND >4, QSU-B >15. Age and education matching was performed using MatchIt package in R with non-parametric nearest neighbor matching, resulting in exclusion of 2 TUD participants. The study applied empirical Bayesian estimation for parameter estimation to enable direct comparison of deviations across cohorts. Scanner artifacts were additionally checked though specific methods not detailed.
